charts.when_to_use: Data has a time axis; user needs to observe rise/fall trends or rate of change over a continuous period
Comparing discrete categories by magnitude; ranking or ordering is the core insight; categories ≤ 15
≤5 categories; one dominant segment vs rest; emphasis on visual proportion over exact values
Exploring relationship between two continuous variables; identifying clusters or outliers in a dataset
Showing intensity/density across a 2D grid; time-based patterns (e.g., activity by hour × day)
Data has a regional/location dimension; spatial distribution is the core insight for the user
Sequential multi-stage process; showing conversion or drop-off rates between defined stages
Single KPI measured against a defined target or threshold; dashboard summary context
Historical data + model predictions; communicating uncertainty range to non-technical stakeholders
Monitoring a time-series for outliers; alerting users to unexpected spikes or dips in operational data
Showing size relationships within a hierarchy; overview of proportional structure (e.g., budget breakdown)
Showing how quantities flow between nodes; multi-source multi-target distribution
Showing how individual positive/negative components add up to a final total (e.g., P&L, budget variance)
Comparing multiple entities across the same fixed set of attributes (e.g., product feature comparison)
Financial time-series with Open/High/Low/Close data; trading or investment product context only
Mapping connections between entities; network topology or social graph exploration context
Showing spread, median, and outliers of a dataset; comparing distributions across multiple groups
Dashboard with multiple KPIs side by side; space-constrained contexts where a gauge is too large
Showing what fraction of a whole is filled; percentage progress in a visually engaging and accessible format
Exploring nested proportions where both hierarchy and relative size matter (e.g., org spend breakdown)
Decomposing a metric into contributing factors; AI-assisted analysis or BI drill-down scenarios
Scientific/engineering context where Z-axis carries essential info not expressible in 2D
Live monitoring dashboards; IoT/ops data updating at ≥1 Hz; user needs current value at a glance
NLP output visualization; exploratory analysis of text corpus sentiment; frequency-weighted keyword overview
Analyzing event logs to visualize actual process flows; identifying bottlenecks and deviations in ops/product funnels

threejs.description: Install the exact current Three.js release with npm for bundler projects. If a browser CDN is unavoidable use an import map pinned to the same exact release instead of a floating URL.
threejs.do: Pin three@0.185.1 and keep core and addon imports on that release
threejs.dont: Use a floating latest URL or a legacy global build as the default production setup
threejs.code_good: npm install three@0.185.1
threejs.code_bad: <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script>

threejs.description: CapsuleGeometry is part of the current Three.js geometry API and directly creates a capsule from radius length cap segments and radial segments.
threejs.do: Construct current capsule meshes with THREE.CapsuleGeometry
threejs.dont: Rebuild a standard capsule from separate cylinder and sphere meshes unless custom topology is required
threejs.code_good: const geometry = new THREE.CapsuleGeometry(0.5, 1, 4, 8); const capsule = new THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);
threejs.code_bad: const body = new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.5, 0.5, 1); // unnecessary multi-mesh workaround

threejs.description: OrbitControls is an addon and must be imported explicitly from the three/addons path while the core library is imported from three.
threejs.do: Import the named OrbitControls addon before constructing controls
threejs.dont: Expect THREE.OrbitControls to exist on the core namespace
threejs.code_good: import * as THREE from 'three'; import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js'; const controls = new OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement);
threejs.code_bad: const controls = new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement); // not exported by the core namespace

threejs.description: When OrbitControls cannot be loaded implement spherical orbit using mousedown/mousemove/mouseup. The key is rotating in spherical coordinates so both horizontal AND vertical drag work correctly.
threejs.do: Rotate camera in spherical coordinates so both axes respond correctly to drag
threejs.dont: Move camera.position.x directly — vertical drag is silently ignored and the orbit is incorrect
threejs.code_good: let dragging = false; let prev = { x: 0, y: 0 }; const radius = camera.position.length(); let theta = 0; let phi = Math.PI / 2; canvas.addEventListener('mousedown', () => dragging = true); canvas.addEventListener('mouseup', () => dragging = false); canvas.addEventListener('mousemove', e => { if (!dragging) return; theta -= (e.clientX - prev.x) * 0.005; phi = Math.max(0.1, Math.min(Math.PI - 0.1, phi - (e.clientY - prev.y) * 0.005)); camera.position.set(radius * Math.sin(phi) * Math.sin(theta), radius * Math.cos(phi), radius * Math.sin(phi) * Math.cos(theta)); camera.lookAt(scene.position); prev = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY }; });
threejs.code_bad: let dragging = false; let prev = { x: 0, y: 0 }; canvas.addEventListener('mousemove', e => { if (!dragging) return; camera.position.x += (e.clientX - prev.x) * 0.005; camera.lookAt(scene.position); prev = { x: e.clientX, y: e.clientY }; }); // BUG: Y-drag ignored; orbit is a horizontal slide not a sphere

threejs.guideline: Use ESM Imports with Bundlers or Import Maps
threejs.description: Import Three.js from three in bundler projects. For a no-build browser page define an exact-version import map for three and three/addons/ before importing modules.
threejs.do: Use one ESM dependency graph with core and addons pinned to the same release
threejs.dont: Mix global script builds with ES module imports or map core and addons to different versions
threejs.code_good: <script type="importmap">{"imports":{"three":"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.185.1/build/three.module.js","three/addons/":"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.185.1/examples/jsm/"}}</script> <script type="module">import * as THREE from 'three'; import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';</script>
threejs.code_bad: <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js"></script><script type="module">import * as THREE from 'three';</script>

threejs.description: Create one WebGLRenderer instance for the lifetime of the page. Multiple renderers compete for the browser GPU context limit (8–16 contexts) and cause context-lost errors especially on mobile.
threejs.do: Reuse a single renderer and swap scene content instead of recreating the renderer
threejs.dont: Create a new renderer on each component mount or scene transition
threejs.code_good: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true }); renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2)); renderer.setSize(canvas.clientWidth, canvas.clientHeight); // renderer lives for the page lifetime
threejs.code_bad: function showScene() { const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer(); document.body.appendChild(renderer.domElement); } showScene(); showScene(); // two GPU contexts — crashes on mobile

threejs.description: Cap devicePixelRatio at 2. Retina displays report 3x or higher. Going from 2x to 3x multiplies pixel count by 2.25x with no visible quality improvement at normal viewing distance.
threejs.do: Apply Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2) — cap is at 2 not at 3
threejs.dont: Pass window.devicePixelRatio directly without any cap
threejs.code_good: renderer.setPixelRatio(Math.min(window.devicePixelRatio, 2));
threejs.code_bad: renderer.setPixelRatio(window.devicePixelRatio); // 3x display = 9 pixels per CSS pixel = 2.25x GPU cost for zero quality gain

threejs.description: Set alpha:true on the renderer and control the background color through CSS rather than a renderer clear color. This composites the canvas correctly over any HTML content behind it.
threejs.do: Set alpha:true on renderer and let body or a parent div provide the background color
threejs.dont: Set a solid renderer clear color when the canvas must composite over HTML behind it
threejs.code_good: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ alpha: true }); renderer.setClearColor(0x000000, 0); // fully transparent canvas // body { background: #0d0d0d; } handles the visible color
threejs.code_bad: renderer.setClearColor(0x111827); // fully opaque — HTML behind the canvas is blocked

threejs.description: Always update camera.aspect and call camera.updateProjectionMatrix() inside every resize handler. A stale aspect ratio causes the entire scene to appear stretched or squashed horizontally.
threejs.do: Update camera.aspect then call updateProjectionMatrix() on every resize
threejs.dont: Let aspect ratio become stale after the browser window changes size
threejs.code_good: window.addEventListener('resize', () => { camera.aspect = canvas.clientWidth / canvas.clientHeight; camera.updateProjectionMatrix(); renderer.setSize(canvas.clientWidth, canvas.clientHeight); });
threejs.code_bad: // No resize handler — scene stretches to fill a wider window without correcting the projection

threejs.description: Use a field of view between 45 and 75 degrees. Below 45 creates compressed telephoto distortion. Above 90 creates visible fisheye distortion at frame edges.
threejs.do: Start at 75 for general interactive scenes; use 45–55 for product close-ups
threejs.dont: Use FOV above 90 or below 30 without a deliberate artistic reason
threejs.code_good: const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, aspect, 0.1, 1000); // general const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(50, aspect, 0.1, 1000); // product shot
threejs.code_bad: const camera = new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(120, aspect, 0.1, 1000); // fisheye distortion at all edges

threejs.description: Always set an explicit camera position and call camera.lookAt() before the first render. The default camera at the origin pointing down -Z makes subjects at arbitrary coordinates invisible or tiny.
threejs.do: Set camera.position.set() and camera.lookAt() to frame the subject before the first render
threejs.dont: Leave the camera at default position (0 0 0) with no lookAt — subject may be behind the camera or microscopic
threejs.code_good: camera.position.set(0, 1.5, 5); camera.lookAt(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0));
threejs.code_bad: // No position or lookAt set — subject at y:2 is behind or above the default camera view

threejs.description: Use OrbitControls for model viewers and exploratory scenes where the user needs free-look. Use a GSAP scroll-driven camera rig for product reveals or storytelling where the camera path must stay fixed.
threejs.do: Import OrbitControls from three/addons and match the camera control approach to the scene's UX intent
threejs.dont: Use OrbitControls for a scripted reveal where users can orbit away before it completes
threejs.code_good: import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js'; const controls = new OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement); controls.enableDamping = true; // call controls.update() in animate()
threejs.code_bad: const controls = new THREE.OrbitControls(camera, renderer.domElement); // legacy global API and wrong control model for a scripted reveal

threejs.description: Creating a new geometry inside animate() allocates a fresh GPU buffer every frame and exhausts VRAM within seconds. Create all geometry exactly once before the loop starts. Use attribute mutation if positions must change per frame.
threejs.do: Create all geometry before the animation loop; mutate BufferAttribute arrays in-place if needed
threejs.dont: Call any new XxxGeometry() constructor inside the animation loop
threejs.code_good: const geo = new THREE.SphereGeometry(1, 32, 32); // created once const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat); scene.add(mesh); const timer = new THREE.Timer(); function animate(timestamp) { requestAnimationFrame(animate); timer.update(timestamp); mesh.rotation.y += timer.getDelta() * 0.8; // delta time renderer.render(scene, camera); }
threejs.code_bad: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); const geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1); // NEW GPU buffer every frame — VRAM exhaustion }

threejs.description: When multiple objects share the same shape create one geometry instance and pass it to every Mesh. Each Mesh gets its own transform and material while all share a single GPU buffer.
threejs.do: Create one geometry and pass the same reference to every Mesh constructor
threejs.dont: Create a separate identical geometry inside a loop for each object
threejs.code_good: const geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1); // one GPU buffer for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) { const m = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat); m.position.set(Math.random() * 10, 0, Math.random() * 10); scene.add(m); }
threejs.code_bad: for (let i = 0; i < 200; i++) { const geo = new THREE.BoxGeometry(1, 1, 1); // 200 separate GPU buffers scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat)); }

threejs.description: Call geometry.dispose() and material.dispose() and texture.dispose() for every texture map when removing objects from the scene. Three.js never releases GPU resources automatically — they stay in VRAM until explicitly freed.
threejs.do: Dispose of geometry + material + every texture map before calling scene.remove()
threejs.dont: Call scene.remove() alone without any dispose calls
threejs.code_good: function removeMesh(mesh) { scene.remove(mesh); mesh.geometry.dispose(); if (mesh.material.map) mesh.material.map.dispose(); if (mesh.material.normalMap) mesh.material.normalMap.dispose(); mesh.material.dispose(); }
threejs.code_bad: scene.remove(mesh); // geometry and all texture maps stay in GPU VRAM forever

threejs.description: Use the minimum segment count that achieves the desired silhouette quality. Hero objects: 32–64 segments. Background objects: 8–16. Particle stand-ins: 6–8. High counts on background geometry waste GPU draw calls with zero visible benefit.
threejs.do: Apply a tiered segment budget based on the visual priority of each object in the scene
threejs.dont: Default every sphere and cylinder to 64+ segments regardless of its role
threejs.code_good: const bgSphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.5, 8, 8); // background const heroSphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(1, 64, 64); // foreground product
threejs.code_bad: const particleSphere = new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.1, 64, 64); // 64 segments × 1000 particles = massive overdraw

threejs.description: For custom shapes use BufferGeometry with typed BufferAttribute data for positions normals colors and other vertex attributes.
threejs.do: Use THREE.BufferGeometry with Float32Array-backed attributes for custom vertex data
threejs.dont: Reference or instantiate the removed THREE.Geometry class
threejs.code_good: const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry(); geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(vertices), 3)); geo.setAttribute('normal', new THREE.BufferAttribute(new Float32Array(normals), 3));
threejs.code_bad: const geo = new THREE.Geometry(); geo.vertices.push(new THREE.Vector3(0, 0, 0)); // removed legacy API

threejs.description: MeshBasicMaterial ignores all lights and is significantly cheaper — use it for UI overlays HUDs and flat-colored decorative elements. MeshStandardMaterial is PBR-accurate and requires lights. Never use StandardMaterial where BasicMaterial suffices.
threejs.do: Use MeshBasicMaterial for any object that does not need lighting; use MeshStandardMaterial for physical objects
threejs.dont: Apply MeshStandardMaterial to flat UI elements that never receive light — lights still run for them
threejs.code_good: const uiMat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0xffffff }); // no lighting cost const physMat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x4f46e5, roughness: 0.4, metalness: 0.6 });
threejs.code_bad: const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0xffffff }); // on a 2D HUD card — lighting calculation runs with no visual benefit

threejs.description: Share one material instance across all meshes that have identical properties. Call mat.clone() only when individual meshes genuinely need different property values. Duplicate materials waste GPU VRAM.
threejs.do: Assign the same material reference to all meshes with identical visual properties
threejs.dont: Create a new material inside a loop for objects that look identical
threejs.code_good: const mat = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x4f46e5, roughness: 0.5 }); meshA.material = mat; meshB.material = mat; meshC.material = mat; // one GPU material
threejs.code_bad: for (const m of meshes) { m.material = new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x4f46e5 }); } // N redundant GPU materials

threejs.description: Textures are the single largest consumer of GPU VRAM in most Three.js scenes. Call texture.dispose() when switching scenes or removing objects — Three.js does not garbage-collect GPU resources automatically.
threejs.do: Track all loaded textures and call dispose() on each one during scene teardown or on object removal
threejs.dont: Load textures without any cleanup path — they persist in VRAM for the entire page lifetime
threejs.code_good: const tex = new THREE.TextureLoader().load('img.jpg'); mesh.material.map = tex; // on teardown: tex.dispose(); mesh.material.dispose();
threejs.code_bad: const tex = new THREE.TextureLoader().load('img.jpg'); scene.remove(mesh); // tex occupies GPU VRAM until page reload

threejs.description: Any scene using MeshStandardMaterial or MeshPhongMaterial requires at minimum one AmbientLight (fill) and one DirectionalLight (shading direction). Without both the objects render as solid black — the material is there but no light reaches it.
threejs.do: Add AmbientLight for fill and DirectionalLight for shading whenever PBR or Phong materials are used
threejs.dont: Use MeshStandardMaterial without adding any lights to the scene
threejs.code_good: scene.add(new THREE.AmbientLight(0xffffff, 0.4)); const dirLight = new THREE.DirectionalLight(0xffffff, 1.0); dirLight.position.set(5, 10, 7.5); scene.add(dirLight);
threejs.code_bad: const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, new THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({ color: 0x4f46e5 })); scene.add(mesh); // renders completely black — no lights in scene

threejs.description: renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true must be set before any castShadow or receiveShadow flags. Without it the shadow map is never allocated and all shadow flags are silently ignored. Keep shadowMap.type at PCFShadowMap (the default): PCFSoftShadowMap is deprecated since r182 and falls back to PCFShadowMap with a console warning. For softer edges raise light.shadow.radius or use VSMShadowMap.
threejs.do: Set renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true first then set castShadow and receiveShadow on lights and meshes
threejs.dont: Set castShadow on a light or mesh without enabling renderer.shadowMap.enabled — shadows never render
threejs.code_good: renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true; renderer.shadowMap.type = THREE.PCFShadowMap; // default dirLight.castShadow = true; dirLight.shadow.mapSize.width = 2048; dirLight.shadow.mapSize.height = 2048; dirLight.shadow.radius = 2; // optional: softer PCF edges heroMesh.castShadow = true; ground.receiveShadow = true;
threejs.code_bad: dirLight.castShadow = true; heroMesh.castShadow = true; // renderer.shadowMap.enabled never set — shadows silently do not render

threejs.description: Shadow map rendering redraws the entire scene from the light's perspective every frame. Enable castShadow only on the primary directional light and receiveShadow only on hero meshes and the ground plane.
threejs.do: Enable shadows only on the key light and the most important meshes
threejs.dont: Enable castShadow and receiveShadow on every object in the scene including particles
threejs.code_good: renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true; renderer.shadowMap.type = THREE.PCFShadowMap; dirLight.castShadow = true; heroMesh.castShadow = true; ground.receiveShadow = true; // particles and background meshes: no shadow flags
threejs.code_bad: for (const m of allMeshes) { m.castShadow = true; m.receiveShadow = true; } // shadow map pass over particle system — expensive with no visible gain

threejs.description: MeshBasicMaterial completely ignores all scene lights. Adding lights solely to illuminate BasicMaterial objects wastes a light pass on every frame with zero visible effect.
threejs.do: Omit lights entirely when every material in the scene is MeshBasicMaterial
threejs.dont: Add AmbientLight and DirectionalLight to a scene that uses only MeshBasicMaterial
threejs.code_good: // Scene uses only MeshBasicMaterial — no lights needed const mat = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial({ color: 0x00ffff }); const mesh = new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat); scene.add(mesh); // MeshBasicMaterial is always fully lit by definition
threejs.code_bad: scene.add(new THREE.AmbientLight(0xffffff, 1.0)); // wasted per-frame light pass — BasicMaterial ignores it entirely

threejs.description: Create exactly one Raycaster instance outside all event handlers. Store mouse coordinates in pointermove (cheap). Call setFromCamera and intersectObjects together inside the animate() loop — once per frame instead of once per mouse event.
threejs.do: Create one Raycaster; store mouse in pointermove; call setFromCamera + intersectObjects inside animate()
threejs.dont: Create a new THREE.Raycaster() inside a mousemove handler or call setFromCamera inside the event listener
threejs.code_good: const raycaster = new THREE.Raycaster(); const mouse = new THREE.Vector2(); canvas.addEventListener('pointermove', e => { // only store coords — no raycasting here mouse.x = (e.clientX / canvas.clientWidth) * 2 - 1; mouse.y = -(e.clientY / canvas.clientHeight) * 2 + 1; }); // setFromCamera and intersectObjects run once per frame in animate()
threejs.code_bad: window.addEventListener('mousemove', e => { const rc = new THREE.Raycaster(); // new allocation per event rc.setFromCamera(mouse, camera); rc.intersectObjects(targets, true); // fires 200+ times/sec });

threejs.description: Raycasting requires mouse in Normalized Device Coordinates: X from -1 (left) to +1 (right) and Y from +1 (top) to -1 (bottom). The Y axis is inverted relative to screen space. A missing negation on Y causes all raycasts to miss or hit the wrong objects.
threejs.do: Apply the full NDC formula — including the negation on the Y axis
threejs.dont: Forget to negate Y — raycasting appears to work but hits objects mirrored vertically
threejs.code_good: mouse.x = (e.clientX / canvas.clientWidth) * 2 - 1; mouse.y = -(e.clientY / canvas.clientHeight) * 2 + 1; // Y is INVERTED
threejs.code_bad: mouse.x = (e.clientX / canvas.clientWidth) * 2 - 1; mouse.y = (e.clientY / canvas.clientHeight) * 2 - 1; // BUG: Y not negated — raycasting is mirrored

threejs.description: Call raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse camera) and then raycaster.intersectObjects(targets true) inside the animate() loop. setFromCamera must come before intersectObjects every frame — without it the raycaster uses a stale ray direction.
threejs.do: Call setFromCamera then intersectObjects in order inside every animate() frame
threejs.dont: Call intersectObjects without calling setFromCamera first — the raycaster uses a stale or zero ray
threejs.code_good: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse, camera); // update ray direction first const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects(targets, true); // then test intersections if (hits.length > 0) { document.body.style.cursor = 'pointer'; } else { document.body.style.cursor = 'auto'; } renderer.render(scene, camera); }
threejs.code_bad: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects(targets, true); // BUG: setFromCamera never called — stale ray — hits is always empty renderer.render(scene, camera); }

threejs.guideline: Recursive Flag for Groups and GLTF
threejs.description: Pass true as the second argument to intersectObjects when testing Groups or GLTF loaded models. Geometry lives on child Mesh objects — without recursive:true the parent group is tested but has no geometry and hits is always empty.
threejs.do: Use intersectObjects(targets true) for Groups or any loaded model
threejs.dont: Raycast against a parent Group without the recursive flag
threejs.code_good: const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects(scene.children, true); // catches all descendant meshes
threejs.code_bad: const hits = raycaster.intersectObjects([modelGroup]); // recursive defaults to false — misses all children

threejs.description: Set document.body.style.cursor = 'pointer' when intersections are found and reset to 'auto' when none are found. Without cursor feedback users cannot discover that 3D objects are interactive.
threejs.do: Update cursor to pointer on hit; reset to auto on miss in the same animate loop block
threejs.dont: Run raycasting and read hits without ever updating the cursor style
threejs.code_good: if (hits.length > 0) { document.body.style.cursor = 'pointer'; } else { document.body.style.cursor = 'auto'; }
threejs.code_bad: raycaster.setFromCamera(mouse, camera); raycaster.intersectObjects(targets, true); // hits ignored — cursor never changes — objects feel non-interactive

threejs.description: Drive the render loop exclusively with requestAnimationFrame or renderer.setAnimationLoop(). Never use setInterval or setTimeout — they are not synchronized to the display refresh rate and keep running when the tab is hidden draining battery.
threejs.do: Use requestAnimationFrame or renderer.setAnimationLoop() as the sole render loop driver
threejs.dont: Use setInterval or setTimeout for render timing
threejs.code_good: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); renderer.render(scene, camera); } animate();
threejs.code_bad: setInterval(() => renderer.render(scene, camera), 16); // not display-synced; runs at full speed even when tab is hidden

threejs.description: Use THREE.Timer and timer.getDelta() for all time-based motion. THREE.Clock is deprecated since r183 and logs a warning. A hardcoded increment like += 0.01 runs at 2x speed on 120Hz displays and at unpredictable speed when frames drop under load. CRITICAL: call timer.update(timestamp) exactly ONCE at the top of every animate() frame before reading the timer. getDelta() and getElapsed() then return stable values for the whole frame and can be read any number of times — skipping update() leaves the delta stale and calling update() twice in one frame makes the second delta ~0.
threejs.do: Call timer.update(timestamp) once at the top of animate(); read timer.getDelta() into dt and reuse dt everywhere in that frame
threejs.dont: Keep using the deprecated THREE.Clock or call timer.update() more than once per frame
threejs.code_good: const timer = new THREE.Timer(); timer.connect(document); // optional: no huge delta after the tab was hidden function animate(timestamp) { requestAnimationFrame(animate); timer.update(timestamp); // ONCE per frame const dt = timer.getDelta(); mesh.rotation.y += dt * 0.8; particles.rotation.y += dt * 0.1; // reuse dt renderer.render(scene, camera); }
threejs.code_bad: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); mesh.rotation.y += 0.01; // 0.01 rad/frame — runs 2x faster on 120Hz than on 60Hz }

threejs.description: Use value += (target - value) * alpha each frame to smoothly interpolate toward a moving target. An alpha of 0.03–0.1 produces organic easing for camera follow pointer-tracking and hover scale effects without requiring GSAP.
threejs.do: Apply the lerp formula each frame with a small alpha for smooth organic motion
threejs.dont: Snap a value directly to the target producing an instant jarring jump
threejs.code_good: // In animate(): cameraTargetX = mouse.x * 3; camera.position.x += (cameraTargetX - camera.position.x) * 0.05; camera.position.y += (cameraTargetY - camera.position.y) * 0.05; camera.lookAt(scene.position);
threejs.code_bad: // In animate(): camera.position.x = mouse.x * 3; // instant snap — jarring with no easing

threejs.description: Use GSAP timelines for any animation with more than two sequential steps or for scroll-linked camera paths. GSAP timelines can be paused reversed and scrubbed — far more maintainable than boolean state machines.
threejs.do: Use GSAP timelines for sequences with more than two steps and for scroll-driven animations
threejs.dont: Implement multi-step sequences with boolean flags and manual frame counters
threejs.code_good: const tl = gsap.timeline({ defaults: { ease: 'power2.out' } }); tl.from(mesh.position, { y: -3, duration: 1 }) .to(mesh.rotation, { y: Math.PI, duration: 1 }, '-=0.3') .to(camera.position, { z: 2, duration: 1.5 });
threejs.code_bad: let step = 0; let t = 0; function animate() { if (step === 0 && (t += 0.01) >= 1) step = 1; } // grows unmanageable with 3+ steps

threejs.guideline: Pause Render Loop on Tab Hidden
threejs.description: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop() as the loop driver so you can pass null to pause and a function to resume. Continuous rendering in a hidden tab wastes CPU GPU and battery with no user benefit.
threejs.do: Use renderer.setAnimationLoop(animate) to drive the loop; pass null to pause on visibilitychange
threejs.dont: Drive with internal requestAnimationFrame and never stop the loop when the tab is hidden
threejs.code_good: const timer = new THREE.Timer(); timer.connect(document); // resets on tab return so the first delta after resume is not huge renderer.setAnimationLoop(animate); // use setAnimationLoop as the driver — not requestAnimationFrame inside animate function animate(timestamp) { timer.update(timestamp); const dt = timer.getDelta(); renderer.render(scene, camera); } document.addEventListener('visibilitychange', () => { if (document.hidden) renderer.setAnimationLoop(null); else renderer.setAnimationLoop(animate); });
threejs.code_bad: function animate() { requestAnimationFrame(animate); // self-referencing RAF cannot be stopped externally renderer.render(scene, camera); } animate(); // runs forever in background tab — drains battery

threejs.description: Load GSAP from its own CDN script tag before your scene script. In bundler projects install via npm and import. GSAP is a completely separate library from Three.js — never try to import it from the Three.js package.
threejs.do: Load GSAP CDN before the scene script; or npm install gsap and import separately
threejs.dont: Import gsap from three or expect it to be defined without a separate load
threejs.code_good: <!-- CDN: load GSAP before your scene script --> <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/gsap/3.12.2/gsap.min.js"></script> <!-- Bundler: --> // import gsap from 'gsap'; import { ScrollTrigger } from 'gsap/ScrollTrigger';
threejs.code_bad: import gsap from 'three'; // undefined — GSAP has nothing to do with Three.js

threejs.description: Call gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) once at the top of your script before any scrollTrigger config object. Without registration the ScrollTrigger name is undefined and the tween throws immediately.
threejs.do: Call gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger) as the first line before any gsap.to/from/timeline with scrollTrigger
threejs.dont: Include scrollTrigger config in gsap.to() calls without first registering the plugin
threejs.code_good: gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger); gsap.to(camera.position, { z: 2, scrollTrigger: { trigger: '.hero-section', scrub: 1 } });
threejs.code_bad: gsap.to(mesh.position, { scrollTrigger: { trigger: '.section', scrub: true } }); // TypeError: ScrollTrigger is not a constructor — not registered

threejs.description: GSAP can tween any numeric JavaScript property including mesh.position.x mesh.rotation.y and material.opacity. No wrapper or adaptor is needed. Note: to tween material.opacity the material must have transparent:true set before the tween starts.
threejs.do: Pass Three.js object properties directly to gsap.to(); set transparent:true before tweening opacity
threejs.dont: Use a plain proxy object then manually copy values to Three.js properties every frame
threejs.code_good: gsap.to(mesh.rotation, { y: Math.PI * 2, duration: 2, ease: 'power1.inOut' }); mesh.material.transparent = true; // required before tweening opacity gsap.to(mesh.material, { opacity: 0, duration: 1 });
threejs.code_bad: const tw = { v: 0 }; gsap.to(tw, { v: Math.PI * 2, onUpdate: () => mesh.rotation.y = tw.v }); // unnecessary proxy wrapper

threejs.description: Use scrub:true or scrub:1 to link camera movement continuously to scroll position as a 0–1 ratio. scrub:1 adds a 1-second lag for cinematic smoothness. onEnter/onLeave fire only once and create jarring snaps — not the right tool for a camera path.
threejs.do: Use scrub:1 for any scroll-controlled camera movement
threejs.dont: Use onEnter or onLeave callbacks for camera motion — they snap instead of scrubbing
threejs.code_good: gsap.registerPlugin(ScrollTrigger); gsap.to(camera.position, { x: 5, y: 2, z: 0, ease: 'none', scrollTrigger: { trigger: '.canvas-wrapper', start: 'top top', end: 'bottom bottom', scrub: 1 } });
threejs.code_bad: gsap.to(camera.position, { z: 0, scrollTrigger: { trigger: '.section', onEnter: () => {} } }); // fires once at scroll threshold — not a continuous scrub

threejs.description: Use THREE.InstancedMesh when rendering 50 or more identical objects. It submits all N transforms in one draw call instead of N draw calls and reduces CPU-GPU communication overhead dramatically.
threejs.do: Use InstancedMesh for any group of 50+ meshes sharing the same geometry and material
threejs.dont: Create 50+ separate Mesh objects with the same geometry and material
threejs.code_good: const COUNT = 500; const iMesh = new THREE.InstancedMesh(geo, mat, COUNT); const matrix = new THREE.Matrix4(); for (let i = 0; i < COUNT; i++) { matrix.setPosition(Math.random()*10, Math.random()*10, Math.random()*10); iMesh.setMatrixAt(i, matrix); } iMesh.instanceMatrix.needsUpdate = true; scene.add(iMesh);
threejs.code_bad: for (let i = 0; i < 500; i++) { scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(geo, mat)); } // 500 separate draw calls per frame

threejs.guideline: Tone Mapping and Output Color Space
threejs.description: Three.js color management is enabled by default. Keep working colors in the linear-sRGB space and set the renderer output color space to SRGBColorSpace; choose tone mapping when rendering HDR lighting to a display.
threejs.do: Use the default ColorManagement.enabled state and set renderer.outputColorSpace plus an appropriate toneMapping
threejs.dont: Disable color management or use removed outputEncoding and sRGBEncoding properties
threejs.code_good: THREE.ColorManagement.enabled = true; renderer.outputColorSpace = THREE.SRGBColorSpace; renderer.toneMapping = THREE.ACESFilmicToneMapping; renderer.toneMappingExposure = 1.0;
threejs.code_bad: renderer.outputEncoding = THREE.sRGBEncoding; // removed legacy properties

threejs.description: The antialias option can only be set at WebGLRenderer construction time. Setting renderer.antialias after construction has absolutely no effect — the WebGL context is already created without it. Decide before instantiating.
threejs.do: Set antialias:true inside the WebGLRenderer constructor options object
threejs.dont: Construct the renderer without antialias then try to enable it by assigning the property
threejs.code_good: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer({ antialias: true, alpha: true }); // antialias baked into the WebGL context
threejs.code_bad: const renderer = new THREE.WebGLRenderer(); renderer.antialias = true; // no effect — context created without AA — edges remain aliased

threejs.guideline: FogExp2 for Depth and Far Culling
threejs.description: Use scene.fog to create atmospheric depth. As a secondary benefit objects that disappear into fog before the far plane stop contributing to draw calls — useful in scenes with large view distances.
threejs.do: Add FogExp2 to scenes with view distances above 100 units for both visual atmosphere and implicit far culling
threejs.dont: Ignore fog in scenes with far:1000+ and many distant objects that contribute tiny pixels per draw call
threejs.code_good: scene.fog = new THREE.FogExp2(0x0a0a0a, 0.02); // exponential — density feels more natural than linear
threejs.code_bad: // far: 2000 with no fog — hundreds of distant objects too small to see still cost draw calls per frame

threejs.guideline: BufferGeometry Plus Points for Particle Systems
threejs.description: Build all particle systems with BufferGeometry plus a Float32Array position attribute rendered as Points. Never use individual Mesh objects as particles — they cannot scale past a few hundred with good performance.
threejs.do: Use Points plus BufferGeometry for all particle effects
threejs.dont: Create hundreds of individual Mesh objects to simulate a particle system
threejs.code_good: const COUNT = 3000; const geo = new THREE.BufferGeometry(); const pos = new Float32Array(COUNT * 3); for (let i = 0; i < COUNT * 3; i++) pos[i] = (Math.random() - 0.5) * 20; geo.setAttribute('position', new THREE.BufferAttribute(pos, 3)); const particles = new THREE.Points(geo, new THREE.PointsMaterial({ size: 0.05, color: 0xffffff })); scene.add(particles);
threejs.code_bad: for (let i = 0; i < 500; i++) { scene.add(new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.SphereGeometry(0.05, 8, 8), mat)); } // 500 separate draw calls per frame

threejs.description: Start particle systems at 1000–3000 particles. Beyond 50000 causes sustained frame drops on mid-range mobile. Always test on a real device before increasing the count — desktop and mobile GPU performance ratios can be 10:1.
threejs.do: Start at 3000 particles and profile on actual mobile hardware before raising the limit
threejs.dont: Set particle count at 100000 or higher without any mobile profiling
threejs.code_good: const COUNT = 3000; // safe mobile baseline — profile before going higher const pos = new Float32Array(COUNT * 3);
threejs.code_bad: const COUNT = 150000; // 60fps on desktop — 8fps on a mid-range Android phone

threejs.description: After mutating any BufferAttribute array values per frame you must set geometry.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true so Three.js re-uploads the changed buffer to the GPU. Without it the GPU still uses the old data and particles appear completely frozen.
threejs.do: Set needsUpdate = true on the position attribute after every per-frame mutation of the array
threejs.dont: Mutate the Float32Array values without flagging needsUpdate — positions update in JS but not on the GPU
threejs.code_good: // In animate() after timer.update(timestamp): const t = timer.getElapsed(); const pos = geo.attributes.position.array; for (let i = 0; i < pos.length; i += 3) { pos[i + 1] += Math.sin(t + i) * 0.001; // Y component } geo.attributes.position.needsUpdate = true; // GPU re-upload
threejs.code_bad: // In animate(): pos[1] += 0.001; // JS array updated — GPU buffer is stale — particles do not move

threejs.description: Size the renderer and camera to the canvas element's clientWidth and clientHeight — not window.innerWidth and innerHeight. This is correct when the canvas is inside a flex or grid container that does not fill the full viewport.
threejs.do: Use canvas.clientWidth and canvas.clientHeight for all renderer and camera sizing
threejs.dont: Hardcode renderer size to window.innerWidth/innerHeight when the canvas may be inside a container
threejs.code_good: renderer.setSize(canvas.clientWidth, canvas.clientHeight); camera.aspect = canvas.clientWidth / canvas.clientHeight; camera.updateProjectionMatrix();
threejs.code_bad: renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight); // wrong when canvas lives inside a sidebar or grid column

threejs.description: Use ResizeObserver on the canvas container instead of the window resize event. ResizeObserver fires when the container element changes size independently of the browser window — common in split-pane layouts and sidebar collapsing.
threejs.do: Attach ResizeObserver to the canvas parent element for accurate container-aware resize detection
threejs.dont: Use only window.addEventListener('resize') for canvas sizing when the canvas is not fullscreen
threejs.code_good: const ro = new ResizeObserver(entries => { const { width, height } = entries[0].contentRect; renderer.setSize(width, height); camera.aspect = width / height; camera.updateProjectionMatrix(); }); ro.observe(canvas.parentElement);
threejs.code_bad: window.addEventListener('resize', () => { renderer.setSize(window.innerWidth, window.innerHeight); }); // misses container-only resize events in split-pane UIs

threejs.description: Add touchstart and touchmove listeners alongside mouse events so the scene remains interactive on mobile. Normalize touch coordinates to the same NDC range as mouse events and pass passive:false on touchmove if you call preventDefault.
threejs.do: Handle both mouse and touch input for any interactive 3D scene
threejs.dont: Add only mouse event listeners and leave touch users with no interaction
threejs.code_good: canvas.addEventListener('touchmove', e => { e.preventDefault(); const t = e.touches[0]; mouse.x = (t.clientX / canvas.clientWidth) * 2 - 1; mouse.y = -(t.clientY / canvas.clientHeight) * 2 + 1; }, { passive: false }); canvas.addEventListener('touchstart', e => { e.preventDefault(); }, { passive: false });
threejs.code_bad: canvas.addEventListener('mousemove', handleMouse); // touch events unhandled — mobile users get no interaction

threejs.description: Check window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') before starting any auto-rotation, particle animation, or camera movement. Users who enable this OS preference have motion sickness or vestibular disorders. IMPORTANT: reading .matches once at page load is a one-time snapshot — if the user changes their OS accessibility setting mid-session the scene will not react. Attach a 'change' listener to the MediaQueryList so noMotion stays in sync at runtime.
threejs.do: Use matchMedia.addEventListener('change') to keep noMotion reactive; gate all auto-animation on the live value
threejs.dont: Read .matches once at startup and never update it — the scene ignores mid-session OS setting changes
threejs.code_good: const mq = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)'); let noMotion = mq.matches; mq.addEventListener('change', e => { noMotion = e.matches; }); // In animate(): if (!noMotion) { mesh.rotation.y += dt * 0.8; particles.rotation.y += dt * 0.1; }
threejs.code_bad: const noMotion = window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches; // one-time snapshot — mid-session OS change is ignored entirely

threejs.description: Add role='img' and a descriptive aria-label to renderer.domElement after appending it to the DOM. Screen readers receive no information from a WebGL canvas — the aria-label is the only description they can announce to users.
threejs.do: Set role='img' and a meaningful aria-label on renderer.domElement before or after appending it

threejs.description: For production install the exact Three.js release from npm and use a bundler such as Vite. Import optional loaders controls and post-processing modules from three/addons so all modules share one version.

threejs.dont: Serve legacy global scripts or import addons from deprecated examples/js paths

threejs.description: Load 3D models using GLTFLoader and traverse gltf.scene to configure castShadow receiveShadow and material overrides on all child Mesh nodes. Calling scene.add(gltf.scene) alone silently skips all shadow and material configuration.
threejs.do: Use GLTFLoader and traverse the entire gltf.scene graph to set up shadows and materials on every Mesh child
threejs.dont: Load a GLTF model and pass gltf.scene directly to scene.add without traversing child meshes
threejs.code_good: import { GLTFLoader } from 'three/addons/loaders/GLTFLoader.js'; const loader = new GLTFLoader(); loader.load('model.glb', gltf => { gltf.scene.traverse(child => { if (child.isMesh) { child.castShadow = true; child.receiveShadow = true; } }); scene.add(gltf.scene); });
threejs.code_bad: loader.load('model.glb', gltf => { scene.add(gltf.scene); // shadows and material setup silently skipped on all children });

threejs.description: Use THREE.LOD to automatically swap high-detail and low-detail geometry as objects move closer or farther from the camera. This maintains frame rate in scenes with many objects spread across a large depth range.
threejs.do: Use THREE.LOD to reduce triangle count on distant objects automatically
threejs.dont: Render the same high-polygon geometry for every object regardless of its distance from the camera
threejs.code_good: const lod = new THREE.LOD(); lod.addLevel(highDetailMesh, 0); // used when < 15 units away lod.addLevel(medDetailMesh, 15); // 15–50 units lod.addLevel(lowDetailMesh, 50); // 50+ units scene.add(lod);

uno.description: Speed up development with live XAML editing

uno.code_bad: Full rebuild for margin tweak

uno.description: Conditional namespaces for platform-specific UI
uno.do: xmlns:android xmlns:ios xmlns:wasm for platform XAML
uno.dont: Shared XAML when platforms need different controls
uno.code_bad: #if in code-behind to set text per platform

uno.guideline: Use partial classes for platform code
uno.description: Separate platform implementations in partial files
uno.do: Partial class files with platform-specific logic
uno.dont: #if directives in shared code for large blocks
uno.code_bad: #if __IOS__ ... #elif __ANDROID__ ... 100-line blocks in shared file

uno.description: Target correct platforms with defines
uno.do: __IOS__ __ANDROID__ __WASM__ __DESKTOP__ for platform checks
uno.dont: Inventing custom symbols or checking OS at runtime
uno.code_bad: if (RuntimeInformation.IsOSPlatform(OSPlatform.Android)) for compile-time choice

uno.description: Keep shared code maximized
uno.do: Abstract platform differences behind interfaces
uno.dont: Duplicating logic across platform files
uno.code_bad: Same 50 lines copy-pasted into iOS and Android partial classes

uno.description: Standard WinUI navigation pattern
uno.do: Frame.Navigate with page types
uno.dont: Manual content swapping
uno.code_bad: contentPresenter.Content = new DetailPage();

uno.description: Type-safe navigation with DI integration
uno.do: Uno.Extensions navigation for complex apps
uno.dont: Manual Frame management in large apps
uno.code_bad: Frame.Navigate with string parsing everywhere

uno.description: SystemNavigationManager.BackRequested works on Android iOS and WASM but is unimplemented on WinAppSDK desktop where calling GetForCurrentView() throws at runtime
uno.do: Subscribe to BackRequested only on platforms that support it or use Uno.Toolkit NavigationBar for cross-platform back UX
uno.dont: Calling SystemNavigationManager.GetForCurrentView() on WinUI 3 desktop without a guard
uno.code_bad: SystemNavigationManager.GetForCurrentView().BackRequested += OnBackRequested; with no platform guard — crashes on Windows desktop

uno.description: Support URI activation across platforms
uno.do: Handle protocol activation and URI routing
uno.dont: Single entry point ignoring activation
uno.code_good: Route URIs to specific pages on activation
uno.code_bad: Ignoring OnLaunched activation args

uno.description: Uno offers both rendering approaches
uno.do: Skia for pixel-perfect cross-platform consistency
uno.dont: Assuming native rendering on all platforms
uno.code_bad: Expecting platform-native controls on Skia targets

uno.description: Uno 5.2+ ships a single Skia Desktop shell that auto-selects X11 Win32 or AppKit per OS — Skia.Gtk Skia.Linux.Framebuffer and Skia.WPF heads are deprecated
uno.do: net10.0-desktop TFM with UnoPlatformHostBuilder for cross-platform desktop
uno.dont: Targeting the legacy Skia.Gtk or Skia.Linux.Framebuffer heads in new projects
uno.code_bad: Per-OS Skia.Gtk Skia.MacOS Skia.Linux.Framebuffer head projects

uno.description: Visual differences exist between renderers
uno.do: Visual testing on each active target platform
uno.dont: Testing only on Windows assuming others match
uno.code_good: Screenshot tests on iOS Android WASM and Desktop
uno.code_bad: Testing only on Windows Desktop

uno.description: Access native APIs through Uno abstractions
uno.do: Native platform APIs via platform-specific code
uno.dont: Avoiding native features for purity
uno.code_good: #if __IOS__ UIKit API call #endif for camera access
uno.code_bad: Pure shared code that avoids using the camera

uno.description: WebAssembly downloads can be large
uno.do: IL linker and AOT for smaller WASM bundles
uno.dont: Default settings for production WASM

uno.description: Defer element creation until needed
uno.do: x:Load=False for hidden panels and tabs
uno.dont: Loading all UI elements upfront
uno.code_bad: Always-loaded Collapsed panels

uno.description: Compiled bindings eliminate runtime reflection — Uno supports x:Bind across iOS Android WASM Skia and Windows targets that compile XAML so prefer it over {Binding} for static well-typed bindings
uno.do: x:Bind for property and event bindings; reserve {Binding} for runtime-typed DataContext scenarios
uno.dont: {Binding} everywhere when x:Bind would compile
uno.code_bad: <TextBlock Text="{Binding Title}"/> for a statically known property

uno.description: Performance characteristics vary by target
uno.do: Platform-specific profiling tools
uno.dont: Assuming desktop perf equals mobile
uno.code_good: Instruments on iOS and Android Profiler on Android
uno.code_bad: Profiling only on Windows

uno.description: Consistent theming across platforms
uno.do: ThemeResource for adaptive colors
uno.dont: Hardcoded colors per platform
uno.code_bad: Background="#FFFFFF"

uno.description: Application.RequestedTheme accepts only ApplicationTheme.Light/Dark — to follow the system theme leave it unset entirely. ElementTheme.Default exists only on FrameworkElement.RequestedTheme not on Application
uno.do: Omit Application.RequestedTheme so the OS theme wins; set Light or Dark explicitly only after a user chooses an override
uno.dont: Setting Application.RequestedTheme="Default" — not a valid ApplicationTheme value and throws at parse time
uno.code_bad: <Application RequestedTheme="Default"> // not a valid ApplicationTheme

uno.description: Override control sub-properties via resources
uno.do: Lightweight styling keys for minor tweaks
uno.dont: Full ControlTemplate for small changes
uno.code_bad: Copying entire ControlTemplate to change one color

uno.description: Theme rendering differs across platforms
uno.do: Visual theme testing on all targets
uno.dont: Assuming themes look identical everywhere
uno.code_good: Screenshot comparison across platforms for themed controls
uno.code_bad: Theming only tested on Windows

uno.do: CommunityToolkit.Mvvm or Prism for MVVM
uno.dont: Code-behind for business logic

uno.do: Uno.Extensions for DI navigation configuration

uno.dont: Static service locators and singletons

uno.code_bad: Business logic in MyApp.Wasm.csproj

uno.description: Enable screen readers across platforms
uno.do: AutomationProperties.Name on interactive controls
uno.dont: Controls without accessible names

uno.code_bad: Only testing with Narrator on Windows

uno.description: Respect user font size preferences
uno.do: Dynamic font scaling for all text
uno.dont: Fixed font sizes ignoring accessibility

uno.description: Test business logic independently
uno.do: xUnit or MSTest on shared ViewModel code
uno.dont: UI testing only
uno.code_bad: Manual testing on each platform

uno.dont: Manual regression testing
uno.code_bad: Manual click-through on each platform

uno.code_good:
index.html:
Loading…
hidden via JS interop after first Frame.Navigate

uno.do: AOT for production WASM builds
uno.dont: Interpreter mode in production
uno.code_bad: Default interpreter mode in production deployment

uno.description: WASM runs in browser sandbox
uno.do: Feature detection for browser APIs
uno.dont: Assuming desktop capabilities in browser
uno.code_bad: #if __WASM__ StorageFile.GetFileFromPathAsync("C:/data") #endif

uno.description: WinUI NavigationView for consistent navigation across platforms
uno.do: NavigationView with MenuItems for app navigation
uno.dont: Custom hamburger menu implementation
uno.code_bad: Custom SplitView with manual toggle button

uno.description: Cross-platform modal dialogs using WinUI API
uno.do: ContentDialog for confirmations and input
uno.dont: Custom overlay Panel as dialog

uno.do: CommandBar with AppBarButtons for toolbar actions
uno.dont: Custom StackPanel toolbar

uno.description: Platform-native toggle control for on/off preferences
uno.do: ToggleSwitch for settings and feature flags
uno.dont: CheckBox for toggle settings

uno.dont: Properties without change notification
uno.code_good: [ObservableProperty] public partial string Title { get; set; }
uno.code_bad: public string Title { get; set; } without notification

uno.description: Collection change notifications for ItemsSources across platforms
uno.do: ObservableCollection<T> for data-bound lists
uno.dont: List<T> for bound ItemsSources
uno.code_bad: List<Item> Items { get; set; } = new();

uno.description: iOS and Android may suspend or terminate the app — WinAppSDK desktop does not raise Suspending so use window Closed for desktop save-state
uno.do: Save state in OnSuspending and restore on activation
uno.dont: Ignoring lifecycle losing user state on mobile
uno.code_good: Application.Current.Suspending += (s, e) => { var d = e.SuspendingOperation.GetDeferral(); SaveState(); d.Complete(); };
uno.code_bad: No suspend handler losing form data on mobile

uno.description: Structured app initialization with DI and configuration
uno.do: IHost builder pattern for app startup and service registration
uno.dont: Manual initialization in App constructor
uno.code_bad: new MainViewModel() in App.xaml.cs constructor

uno.guideline: Use ListView virtualization for large lists
uno.description: Only renders visible items to reduce memory and layout cost
uno.do: ListView with default ItemsStackPanel virtualization
uno.dont: ItemsControl or StackPanel for large data sets
uno.code_bad: <ItemsControl><StackPanel> rendering 5000 items at once

uno.description: Skia and WinAppSDK targets need full keyboard operability — note TabIndex routing is not fully implemented on every Uno target
uno.do: AccessKey and KeyboardAccelerator on Skia and WinAppSDK targets
uno.dont: Mouse-only interactions on desktop
uno.code_bad: Clickable controls without keyboard support on desktop

uno.guideline: Use service workers for offline support
uno.description: Enable PWA capabilities for WASM deployments
uno.do: Service worker registration for caching and offline mode
uno.dont: Online-only WASM app with no offline fallback
uno.code_bad: No service worker leaving WASM app unusable offline

uno.guideline: Marshal to UI thread with DispatcherQueue
uno.description: Cross-thread access to UI elements throws — capture the UI DispatcherQueue once and use TryEnqueue to update from background work
uno.do: DispatcherQueue.GetForCurrentThread().TryEnqueue from background work
uno.dont: Touching UI controls directly from a Task
uno.code_bad: await Task.Run(() => StatusText.Text = "Done"); throws on non-UI thread

uno.description: Required for Fluent control styles to load — without it controls render with no template
uno.do: Add XamlControlsResources at the top of Application.Resources MergedDictionaries
uno.dont: Skipping the merged dictionary and wondering why Buttons look unstyled
uno.code_bad: <Application.Resources><SolidColorBrush x:Key="MyBrush" Color="Red"/></Application.Resources> with no XamlControlsResources merged

uno.description: AsyncRelayCommand reports CanExecute=false (raising CanExecuteChanged) and exposes IsRunning while the Task is in flight — the bound control is disabled and re-entrancy is prevented by default (AllowConcurrentExecutions=false)
uno.do: [RelayCommand] on a Task-returning method for awaitable work
uno.dont: async void event handlers calling .Wait() or .Result
uno.code_good: [RelayCommand] private async Task LoadAsync() { Items = await _api.GetAsync(); }
uno.code_bad: public void OnLoadClick(object s, EventArgs e) { LoadAsync().Wait(); } deadlock risk

uno.description: WinUI x:Uid resolves UI text from .resw resources at runtime — use it instead of hardcoded strings to support localization across iOS Android WASM and desktop from a single project
uno.do: x:Uid on every user-facing string with matching .resw entries per language under Strings/{lang}/Resources.resw
uno.dont: Hardcoding language-specific strings into XAML or code-behind
uno.code_bad: <Button Content="Submit"/> hardcoded in XAML

uno.description: Cross-platform logging routes to platform-native sinks (OSLog on iOS Console on WASM Debug elsewhere) when configured through the IHost builder
uno.do: Inject ILogger<T> into ViewModels and services and call UseLogging() on the host builder
uno.dont: Console.WriteLine or platform-specific log APIs scattered across shared code
uno.code_good: Host.CreateDefaultBuilder().UseLogging(c => c.SetMinimumLevel(LogLevel.Information)) and ILogger<MainViewModel> via constructor injection
uno.code_bad: Console.WriteLine("error") in shared code with no platform-aware routing

uno.description: Skia Desktop on .NET 10 supports Native AOT for faster cold start and smaller deployments — opt in per-target so debug builds remain fast
uno.do: <PublishAot>true</PublishAot> in a TFM-conditional PropertyGroup for net10.0-desktop release builds
uno.dont: Enabling PublishAot globally and breaking debug iteration on every TFM
uno.code_bad: <PublishAot>true</PublishAot> at root with no TFM/Configuration condition

uno.guideline: Never block on async with .Result or .Wait()
uno.description: Blocking on a Task from the UI thread deadlocks because the awaiter cannot resume on the captured SynchronizationContext — always await async APIs through to the event handler
uno.do: Await async methods all the way up; in libraries call ConfigureAwait(false) to avoid context capture
uno.dont: Calling .Result .Wait() or GetAwaiter().GetResult() on a Task from the UI thread
uno.code_good: private async void OnLoadClick(object s, RoutedEventArgs e) { var data = await _api.GetAsync(); Items = data; }
uno.code_bad: private void OnLoadClick(object s, RoutedEventArgs e) { var data = _api.GetAsync().Result; } // deadlocks on UI thread

uno.guideline: Define ThemeDictionaries for Light Dark and HighContrast
uno.description: Resources placed inside ResourceDictionary.ThemeDictionaries entries are automatically swapped when the system theme changes — required for theme-aware brushes
uno.do: Wrap brushes in a ThemeDictionaries dictionary keyed by Light Dark and HighContrast in App.xaml or page resources
uno.dont: Defining a single brush at the root and missing dark/high-contrast variants
uno.code_bad: <SolidColorBrush x:Key="Brand" Color="#005A9E"/> at root with no theme variants

uno.description: Uno.Sdk is the modern single-project SDK that auto-resolves Uno.WinUI Uno.Toolkit Material and other packages from a UnoFeatures property — declare features by name instead of hand-managing dozens of PackageReferences
uno.do: Declare features in the csproj via <UnoFeatures>...</UnoFeatures> and let the SDK resolve transitive packages
uno.dont: Hand-adding every Uno.* PackageReference and matching version numbers across packages
uno.code_bad: <PackageReference Include="Uno.WinUI"/><PackageReference Include="Uno.Material.WinUI"/> ... duplicated per feature with mismatched versions

uno.guideline: Persist desktop window state via Window.Closed
uno.description: WinAppSDK and Skia desktop heads do not raise Application.Suspending — handle the Window.Closed event (and AppWindow size/position changes) to save user state when desktop apps shut down
uno.do: Subscribe to MainWindow.Closed and persist any unsaved state before the window is destroyed
uno.dont: Relying on Application.Suspending to fire on desktop targets
uno.code_bad: Application.Current.Suspending += SaveState; // never fires on WinAppSDK or Skia desktop

uno.guideline: Use WinRT.Interop for native window handle on Windows
uno.description: Calling Win32 APIs from a WinUI Window (file pickers icon embedding etc.) requires the HWND — retrieve it via WinRT.Interop.WindowNative.GetWindowHandle and guard the call so non-Windows targets stay unaffected
uno.do: GetWindowHandle inside a #if WINDOWS block when you need the HWND
uno.dont: Calling WinRT.Interop in shared code without a platform guard
uno.code_bad: var hWnd = WinRT.Interop.WindowNative.GetWindowHandle(MainWindow); // breaks build on iOS Android WASM
